The backlog contains items of varying detail and form. Ultimately it is a list of work items such as features, functions, requirements, enhancements, experiments and fixes that are currently deemed necessary to deliver the work that are referred to as Backlog Items.

There are varying levels of granularity within a backlog; items at the top of the backlog that the team has committed to delivering soon will likely have greater detail than those scheduled farther out. The lower ordered, and typically less detailed, items that are further down in the backlog and will be elaborated or decomposed into smaller items as they rise to the top.

The backlog evolves as delivery progresses and is influenced by factors such as changes in requirements, user feedback and market conditions. The dynamic nature of the backlog allows it to easily reflect changes in requirements, thereby maximizing the value being delivered. However, this also means that the backlog is a living artifact requiring continuous maintenance, typically done by a single empowered person.

Typically, work items in the Sprint Backlog reflect those of the highest priority from the Product Backlog that have been committed to by the team for a given sprint. These work items are also the ones that will result in fulfilment of the sprint goal.

The Sprint Backlog should always reflect the latest work, which can change at the discretion of the team responsible for development. The latest list of work in the Sprint Backlog must also have the latest estimates thereby representing a clear picture of all remaining work and the likelihood of achieving the sprint goal.

• The backlog should be highly visible and easily accessible
  • The number of items that can be completed by the end of the project or release depends on the overall / team velocity, the number of iterations and the number of teams
  • All items in backlog should be ordered to maximize business value delivered
  • All items in the backlog should be estimated to forecast the completion
  • Incomplete items could be left in the backlog if the team is disbanded
  • The backlog should not be confused with a "requirements document"
To provide transparency about the subset of work committed to by the team in order to satisfy the sprint goal.

Without the Sprint Backlog to guide work, there may be:

  • Duplication of work by team members
  • Lack of visibility on required work to be conducted
  • Missing tasks leading to incomplete work
  • Inappropriate allocation of work
  • Missed dependencies between work items
  • Inaccurate forecasts of when work will be completed, if any forecasts made at all
  • Difficulty managing stakeholder expectations
  • Discrepancies in tracking progress against the sprint goal
Each item on the backlog will have an order that determines the appropriate placing of the item in the overall backlog, no two items can be equally important.

• Tools - May be used to capture the Backlog electronically, especially when teams are distributed. Some common tools include Visual studio, Atlassian JIRA, Trello or Agile Central.
  • Story mapping - A story map consists of Backlog Items arranged along two independent dimensions. The map arranges user activities along the horizontal (X) axis in rough order of priority. Down the vertical (Y) axis is more complex functionality. A set of Backlog Items consisting of the first few items chosen in each column/step represents a "walking skeleton", which may sometimes also be the Minimum Viable Product. Working through successive vertical items provides additional functionality.
  • Storyboards (e.g. Kanban Board) - In its most basic form, a storyboard can be drawn on a whiteboard or even a section of wall. Using electrical tape or a dry erase pen the board is divided into three columns labeled "To Do", "In Progress" and "Done". Many variations exist and different layouts can be used. For instance, additional columns may be used to represent an activity, such as "In Test". The task board is updated frequently, most commonly during the daily meeting, based on the team's progress since the last update. The board is commonly "reset" at the beginning of each iteration to reflect the iteration plan.
